translation_notes: Two one-step traversals in this region, both translated: ks = [t for t in ab.objects(i, RDF.type) if t in kind_cls] -> [t for t in m{ {i} rdf:type ?t } if t in kind_cls], and notes = list(ab.objects(i, SEM.instanceKindNote)) -> list(m{ {i} sem:instanceKindNote ?n }). Also translated the subjects()-direction one-step read insts = set(ab.subjects(SEM.hasSourceProvenance, None)) -> set(m{ ?s sem:hasSourceProvenance [] }): a blank node in object position is the 'match but do not project' wildcard (confirmed non-BNode terms, both a URIRef and a Literal, match it in the fixture) -- the direct counterpart of rdflib's object=None.

SEM[f'Kind{k}'] (bracket indexing on a Namespace, computed local part) becomes sem:{f'Kind{k}'}: terms.md's 'local part may itself be interpolated' form, not seen in the other two regions of this batch.

categories in this meta.json undercount the region: only 'namespace_term' is listed, but the region reads a graph through two rdflib calls (ab.objects, ab.subjects) plus one more in its immediate context (ab.subjects for insts). Matches the known gap (INSTRUCTIONS_403 SS5, 'lectures sans ilot dedie avant m{ }'): ab is a bare module-level name with no type annotation, so the classifier that produced rdf_ops/categories did not recognise it as a graph.

meta.oracle is 'isomorphism', and the harness's module-state comparison (rdfeval/harness.py, entry=None) now compares every comparable module-level value, not just graphs -- bad, ks, notes, insts and kind_cls are all directly compared. Checked this is load-bearing (not a hollow green from the untouched `ab` alone) by deliberately mistranslating the ks pattern during review: the verdict failed on bad/ks/stdout together. See driver.py.

Context-extraction findings, both documented at length in original.py: (1) three of the twelve 'context' lines this region's meta.json context array listed are not really this region's context -- two bare 'bad = []' resets and an os.walk comprehension sit textually AFTER the region in the source file (its own later gates), not before it; (2) the extractor also missed 'from rdflib import Graph, Namespace', despite Graph()/Namespace(...) being used by lines it did keep. Both look like defects in the corpus/404 context-extraction tooling, not a language limitation -- worth a look by whoever maintains it.
